newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE concerned by violence in Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: OSCE concerned by violence in Belgrade.

text.p: Europe's top security body, the OSCE , on Tuesday criticised the use of violence by Yugoslav authorities to break up protests in Belgrade and called on the government to enter into talks with opposition groups.

"The authorities in Belgrade have recently resorted to the use of force and arrests in order to prevent the opposition from peaceful demonstrations. The Chairman-in-Office must express his deep concern and dismay at this development," Danish Foreign Minister and OSCE chairman Niels Helveg Petersen said in a statement released in Copenhagen and obtained by Reuters in Vienna.
OSCE concerned by violence in Belgrade

The OSCE repeated its call for President Slobodan Milosevic to recognise opposition wins in local elections and to begin talks with the opposition on future democratic reforms, possibly under the auspices of the OSCE.

"The Chairman-in-Office calls on the authorities to immediately stop the use of force and to fully and speedily implement the recommendations made by the OSCE concerning the local elections in Serbia," the statement said.

"He also calls on the authorities to engage in a constructive dialogue with representatives of the opposition...The OSCE Chairmanship has repeatedly offered to facilitate such a dialogue," it continued.
Pro-democracy demonstrations in Belgrade entered their 77th day on Monday. Police have used force to break up the rallies but the opposition has vowed to press on with its campaign.
